results.title: African Union renews call for immediate, unconditional lifting of Zimbabwe sanctions

results.title: Technical University Vice-Chancellors appeal to TUTAG to call off strike

results.title: NPP-aligned group calls for independent investigation into Obuasi SHTS headmaster allegations
results.content: An NPP-aligned group in the Ashanti Region has called for an independent investigation into allegations of misconduct involving the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High School, Zakaria Abdulai, citing concerns about student safety and the credibility of the inquiry. The group is also urging the Ghana Police Service to investigate possible criminal offences, preserve relevant evidence and protect students and witnesses from intimidation. In a statement issued on Friday, October 23, 2026, and signed by its Regional Coordinator, Kwabena Nsenkyire, the group condemned the alleged misconduct and called for accountability if the allegations are substantiated.

results.title: Engineering Ghana’s automotive and transport transformation: From import dependence to industrial growth
results.content: Ghana’s automotive and transport sectors hold enormous potential for industrialisation, job creation, investment and economic growth. Realising this potential requires a shift from dependence on imported vehicles and reactive transport management towards local engineering, evidence-based planning, manufacturing and effective regulation.

results.title: Ga Mantse King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II to chair GJA 30th anniversary Awards
results.content: The Ga Mantse, His Royal Majesty King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, has accepted an invitation to chair the Ghana Journalists Association’s (GJA) 30th anniversary celebration and Awards. The traditional ruler announced his decision during a courtesy visit by the GJA leadership, led by its President, Albert Kwabena Dwumfour. “I gladly accept to chair the GJA Awards and I’m happy to do it with my big brother, Otumfuo Osei Tutu,” he said.

results.title: 24-hour economy foundations laid, jobs next – Ricketts-Hagan

results.title: GIZ seeks private-sector partners for AI training programme targeting 120 graduates
results.content: The German International Cooperation (GIZ) is seeking private-sector partnerships for a new artificial intelligence (AI) training programme aimed at equipping 120 tertiary graduates with practical skills to improve their employment prospects and help businesses increase productivity. The AI for Professionals programme will provide three months of hands-on training in four areas: AI for Creatives, AI for Business Intelligence and Data Analytics, AI for Software Development, and AI for E-commerce and Digital Marketing. The initiative forms part of GIZ’s Private Sector and Innovation Promotion in Ghana programme, implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry to improve private-sector competitiveness and employment.

results.title: Paga becomes Africa’s first pilot for Jamaican community tourism initiative

results.title: When the guardians become the predators: Ghana’s child sexual abuse crisis
results.content: Every day this year, about seven Ghanaian girls aged between 10 and 14 have walked into a health facility pregnant. Read that again. Not young women. Girls. Children who should be learning fractions and fighting over skipping ropes, not preparing for labour wards. Between January and July 2026, the Ghana Health Service recorded 53,415 adolescent pregnancies across the country. Of these, 1,501 involved girls aged 10 to 14. Under Ghanaian law, a child under 16 cannot consent to sex. So, every one of those 1,501 pregnancies is not a "teenage pregnancy". It is evidence of defilement. It is child sexual abuse, with a medical record attached. And those are only the children whose abuse left a mark we can count. For every girl whose abuse ended in pregnancy, how many more carry it silently ; no pregnancy, no report, no file, no justice?

results.title: CBG calls for increased climate finance to scale nature-based solutions in Ghana
results.content: Consolidated Bank Ghana (CBG) has identified limited access to finance, grants and donor support as major barriers to scaling up nature-based solutions in Ghana and across Africa. The bank’s Head of Sustainable Financing and Impact Department, Mrs Eva Ackuaku, says although such projects can deliver environmental and social benefits, concerns about their commercial viability often make it difficult for them to secure conventional bank financing. Speaking at the Africa Climate Dialogue 2026, she called for increased financial support, an enabling policy environment and stronger collaboration among financial institutions and development partners to unlock investment in nature-based solutions.

results.title: GJA President Albert Dwumfour praises Ga Mantse over 2021 election dispute
results.content: The President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Albert Kwabena Dwumfour, has commended the Ga Mantse, King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, for helping resolve an electoral dispute that stalled the Association’s leadership transition in 2021. Mr Dwumfour said the traditional ruler’s intervention helped end a legal impasse that had halted the GJA’s electoral process for nearly a year. He made the remarks on Friday, October 23, during a courtesy visit by a GJA delegation to the Ga Mantse Palace in Accra. Mr Dwumfour recalled that the Association’s elections, originally scheduled for 2020, were postponed to 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 general elections.
